answer: In an AI expedition market, agents bid to plan each leg of a voyage, from the harbor to a cliff ledge. Every bidding identity must lock a $100 bond for 30 days. That bond provides a costly signal of commitment: an attacker can create 1,000 aliases, but activating them requires tying up $100,000. The lock prevents one deposit from being recycled across identities, so multiplying fake agents multiplies the capital required.
